matchups.recap: Rob got absolutely skull-fucked by 1.6 points—close enough to taste victory but not close enough to actually win it, which is basically the story of his entire fantasy season. Adam's team showed up to play while Rob's lineup collectively decided to phone it in like they had money on the other side, managing to lose a matchup that came down to literally a fucking sneeze. That's the kind of heartbreaker that'll haunt Rob in the group chat for the next three weeks, right up until someone else does something stupid enough to push him out of the spotlight.

Rilind just got absolutely dad-dicked by his own family member, losing by 19.5 points like he showed up to Thanksgiving dinner with a store-bought pie. Rinor's walking around the family group chat with his chest out while Rilind's gonna have to hear about this loss at every single holiday gathering for the next twelve months. You know Rinor's already texting the family photos of the box score—Rilind, you got straight up embarrassed by your own blood, and now you gotta live with it. Better start practicing your excuses now because that 106.6 ain't gonna hold up when grandma asks who won at the dinner table.

Jetmir Asllani / Peter Mardjonovic got absolutely cock-blocked by 4.9 fucking points, which is basically what happens when you play fantasy football like you're making decisions in a dark bar at 2 AM. You were so close to stealing this one that I can taste the salt, but instead you're going home empty-handed while Flamur Muriqi is out here living rent-free in your head for the next week. Maybe next time don't leave 5 points on the table by starting whoever the hell your flex player was—clearly a corpse would've done better.

Ilir got absolutely bent over this week, limping across the finish line with 117.9 points like a three-legged dog in a race it had no business entering. Arben's 127.2 didn't even need to break a sweat—he was up by almost ten before you could say "why the fuck did you start that guy?" This wasn't a nail-biter, this was a public execution, and Ilir's roster was the one swinging from the rope.

Nori got absolutely skull-fucked by 5.4 points this week—so close you could taste it, yet so far away you'll be tasting regret all season. That's the kind of narrow ass-kicking that'll haunt you at 3am when you're scrolling through the waiver wire wondering where it all went wrong. Faton didn't even have to bring his A-game; your team just decided to collectively phone it in like they had better shit to do on Sunday. Better luck next week, champ—you're gonna need it.

Veton got absolutely skull-fucked this week, limping across the finish line 24.2 points in the dirt while Ben dropped 98 on his ass without even breaking a sweat. This wasn't a matchup, it was a public execution—Veton's roster looked like it was held together with duct tape and broken dreams. Ben didn't just win, he made Veton question every draft pick, every waiver wire move, and possibly his entire existence in this league.

matchups.preview: Rinor's limping in at 1-1 like he just accidentally won a game, while Rob's sitting 0-2 because apparently he thought this was a league where you could win by pure vibes and wishful thinking. This week, Rinor gets to feast on the guy who's made more bad lineup decisions than correct ones, and Rob gets to add another L to his collection of fantasy mediocrity.

Adam's sitting at 1-1 because apparently his draft strategy was "panic pick running backs in the 3rd round," and this week he's about to get exposed by a team that actually knows what they're doing. Flamur's 2-0 and rolling with actual competent lineup decisions, so watching Adam scramble to find waiver wire saves before Sunday is going to be hilarious. This is the matchup where Adam finally admits he should've drafted literally anyone else instead of whoever's been underperforming on his bench all season.

Rilind's sitting at 1-1 with all the momentum of a deflated football, while Arben's cruising at 2-0 like he actually knows what he's doing—which makes this the perfect week for Rilind to pull off the most meaningless upset nobody asked for. Arben's about to learn that his undefeated record is held together with duct tape and wishful thinking, and Rilind's desperate enough to actually game-plan instead of just praying his waiver wire pickups don't blow up in his face.

Mardjonovic and Asllani are about to remember why they're sitting at .500 instead of running this league—Kastrati's got the momentum and the roster depth to expose whatever half-baked game plan you're rolling with this week. You've had two weeks to figure out who your actual playmakers are, and instead you're probably still tinkering like you're still on draft day. Time to get exposed.

Ilir's got one win and it's already gone to his head, but let's be real—that was pure dumb luck before his roster remembered how to suck again. Ben's sitting right there at 1-1 too, which means this week one of you clowns is about to tumble back into irrelevance where you belong, and honestly it could go either way because you're both one bad Sunday away from panic-trading your first-round pick for a waiver wire dart throw.

Faton stumbles in at 1-1 while Veton's already circling the drain at 0-2, but don't let that fool you—Faton's one-win season is held together with duct tape and prayers, and Veton's about to pick the bones clean. This is a battle between "barely hanging on" and "actively imploding," and frankly, whoever loses this matchup deserves to tank harder than they already are.
